**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam).

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** Which statement about empirical and molecular formulas is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ The molecular formula is always a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula\
b)\ The empirical formula gives the actual number of atoms in one molecule\
c)\ The empirical formula is always different from the molecular formula\
d)\ An empirical formula may contain fractional subscripts such as CH~1.5~\
e)\ Two different compounds can never have the same empirical formula

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**2.** Hexane has the molecular formula C~6~H~14~. What is its empirical formula?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ CH~2~\
b)\ C~2~H~5~\
c)\ C~6~H~14~\
d)\ C~3~H~7~\
e)\ C~3~H~8~

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

b)\ N~2~O~5~\
c)\ NO~3~\
d)\ N~4~O~10~\

b)\ C~8~H~20~\

**7.** A gaseous hydrocarbon is 85.63% C and 14.37% H by mass, and its molar mass is 28.05 g/mol. It burns completely in O~2~ to form CO~2~ and H~2~O. How many moles of O~2~ are needed to burn 0.500 mol of the hydrocarbon?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.167 mol\
b)\ 0.500 mol\
c)\ 0.750 mol\
d)\ 1.00 mol\
e)\ 1.50 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**8.** The **limiting reactant** in a chemical reaction is the reactant that:

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ is left over when the reaction stops\
b)\ is completely used up first and so determines how much product can form\
c)\ has the fewest moles present\
d)\ has the smallest coefficient in the balanced equation\
e)\ has the smallest mass

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**9.** Air bags inflate by the reaction 2NaN~3~(s) $\rightarrow$ 2Na(s) + 3N~2~(g). How many moles of N~2~ form from 1.50 mol of NaN~3~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 1.00 mol\
b)\ 1.50 mol\
c)\ 2.25 mol\
d)\ 9.00 mol\
e)\ 63.0 mol

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**12.** Silicon reacts with chlorine according to the **unbalanced** equation Si(s) + Cl~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ SiCl~4~(l). What mass of Cl~2~ is needed to react completely with 7.00 g of Si?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.498 g\
b)\ 8.83 g\
c)\ 14.0 g\
d)\ 17.7 g\
e)\ 35.3 g

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**13.** Methane burns: CH~4~(g) + 2O~2~(g) $\rightarrow$ CO~2~(g) + 2H~2~O(g). A mixture of 8.00 g of CH~4~ and 24.0 g of O~2~ reacts. Which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 1.98 g of CH~4~ is left over\
b)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 6.02 g of CH~4~ is left over\
c)\ Neither is limiting; both reactants are used up completely\
d)\ O~2~ is limiting, and 8.00 g of CH~4~ is left over\
e)\ CH~4~ is limiting, and O~2~ is left over

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

b)\ 15.0 g\
c)\ 23.0 g\
d)\ 25.0 g\

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ 0.929%\
b)\ 46.5%\
c)\ 58.6%\
d)\ 92.9%\
e)\ 108%
